question: How often must an NBFC carry out periodic KYC updation for high-risk customers?
expected_answer: At least once every two years
evidence_quote: the NBFC shall carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers

question: How often must periodic KYC updation be done for medium-risk and low-risk customers?
expected_answer: At least once every eight years for medium-risk and once every ten years for low-risk customers
evidence_quote: once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers

question: Before periodic KYC updation is due how many advance notices must be sent to the customer and in what form?
expected_answer: At least three advance intimations including at least one by letter
evidence_quote: Prior to the due date of periodic updation of KYC, the NBFC shall give at least three advance intimations, including at least one intimation by letter, at appropriate intervals to its customers

question: If an NBFC downloads a customer's KYC record from CKYCR does it need to re-verify the customer's identity and address?
expected_answer: No as long as the downloaded record is current and compliant with the PML Act and Rules; the entity that last uploaded or updated the record is responsible for verification
source_section: para 4(1) (inserts Explanation to para 63) | Chapter X, para 63(9), Explanation
evidence_quote: any NBFC downloading and relying on such records from the CKCYR shall not be required to re-verify the authenticity of the customer's identity and / or address

question: What is the minimum cooling-off period for digital loans?
expected_answer: At least one day. The NBFC sets the exact period in its credit policy.
evidence_quote: The cooling off period shall be determined by the NBFC in terms of their credit policy, subject to the period so determined not being less than one day.

question: Where are the digital lending rules for NBFCs located now?
expected_answer: In Chapter III (Digital Lending) of the RBI (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions 2025
evidence_quote: Digital lending by an NBFC involving a LSP, shall be carried out under a contractual agreement between the NBFC and the LSP
auto_check: fail: answer numbers not in quote: 2025

question: Is the Master Direction on KYC 2016 still in force?
expected_answer: No. Per RBI's Master Directions list (recorded in data/metadata.csv), it was repealed on 28 November 2025 and replaced by entity-wise KYC directions; for NBFCs it is the RBI (NBFC – KYC) Directions 2025.
evidence_quote: Repealed on 2025-11-28 and split into 10 entity-wise KYC directions

question: What relief did the June 2025 KYC amendment give to low-risk individual customers?
expected_answer: Allowed transactions to continue and KYC updation within one year of it falling due or up to 30 June 2026 whichever is later with regular monitoring
source_section: para 4(i) (new clause in para 38 of the 2016 direction)
evidence_quote: KYC within one year of its falling due for KYC or upto June 30, 2026, whichever is later. The RE shall subject accounts of such customers to regular monitoring.

question: What must the Key Facts Statement disclose additionally for digital loans?
expected_answer: (i) The cooling-off/look-up period during which the borrower is not charged any penalty on prepayment of the loan; (ii) details of the LSP acting as recovery agent and authorised to approach the borrower.
evidence_quote: Cooling off / look-up period, in terms of the RE's board approved policy, during which borrower shall not be charged any penalty on prepayment of loan (ii) Details of LSP acting as recovery agent

question: What are the KYC requirements for opening an account for a cryptocurrency exchange?
expected_answer: Not covered in the provided RBI documents
evidence_quote: none

question: What is the maximum Default Loss Guarantee (DLG) cover an NBFC can accept on a loan portfolio?
expected_answer: 5% of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio, at any given time.
evidence_quote: the total amount of DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio which is specified upfront shall not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time.

question: Within what overdue period must an NBFC invoke a DLG?
expected_answer: Within a maximum of 120 days overdue, unless the borrower clears the dues before that.
evidence_quote: An NBFC shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that.

question: If an NBFC does not reply to a digital lending complaint, after how many days can the borrower go to the RBI Complaint Management System?
expected_answer: 30 days from the NBFC receiving the complaint.
evidence_quote: or the borrower has not received any reply within 30 days of receipt of complaint by the NBFC, the said borrower can lodge a complaint over the Complaint Management System

question: If borrower data is processed outside India, how soon must it be brought back to India?
expected_answer: Within 24 hours of processing; it must also be deleted from the servers outside India.
evidence_quote: in case the data is processed outside India, the same shall be deleted from servers outside India and brought back to India within 24 hours of processing.

question: What type of entity must an LSP be to provide a DLG to an NBFC?
expected_answer: A company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013.
evidence_quote: the LSP providing DLG shall be incorporated as a company under the Companies Act, 2013.

question: Can an NBFC automatically increase a digital borrower's credit limit?
expected_answer: No. Only if the borrower explicitly requests it, and the request is evaluated and kept on record.
evidence_quote: An NBFC shall ensure that there is no automatic increase in credit limit unless an explicit request is received, evaluated and kept on record from the borrower for such increase.

question: Who pays the fees and charges due to a Lending Service Provider (LSP)?
expected_answer: The NBFC pays them directly. The LSP cannot charge or collect them from the borrower.
evidence_quote: An NBFC shall ensure that any fees, charges, reimbursements, etc. payable to LSP are paid directly by the NBFC and are not charged to or collected from the borrowers separately by LSP.

question: Can an NBFC or its LSP collect or store a digital borrower's biometric data?
expected_answer: No, unless allowed under existing statutory guidelines.
evidence_quote: An NBFC shall ensure that no biometric data is stored / collected by the NBFC and LSP, unless allowed under extant statutory guidelines.

question: Once an NBFC invokes a DLG, can the DLG amount be reinstated if the loan is later recovered?
expected_answer: No. An invoked DLG amount is never reinstated, including through loan recovery.
evidence_quote: DLG amount once invoked by an NBFC shall not be reinstated, including through loan recovery.

question: For a company customer, what shareholding makes a person a beneficial owner under the NBFC KYC Directions?
expected_answer: Owning or being entitled to more than 10% of the company's shares, capital or profits (or exercising control by other means).
evidence_quote: ownership of / entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company.

question: Within how many days must an NBFC upload a new customer's KYC records to CKYCR?
expected_answer: Within 10 days of starting the account-based relationship.
evidence_quote: the NBFC shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

question: How often must an NBFC review the risk categorisation of customer accounts?
expected_answer: At least once every six months.
evidence_quote: The NBFC shall put in place a system of periodic review of risk categorisation of accounts, with such periodicity being at least once in every six months

question: What is the maximum loan an NBFC can sanction in a year to a customer onboarded through Aadhaar OTP e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode?
expected_answer: Only term loans, up to Rs 60,000 in total in a year.
evidence_quote: As regards borrowal accounts, the NBFC shall sanction only term loans. The aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed ₹60,000 in a year.

question: During V-CIP, how old can the Aadhaar XML file or Secure QR code be?
expected_answer: Not older than three working days from the date of the V-CIP.
evidence_quote: the NBFC shall ensure that the XML file or QR code generation date is not older than three working days from the date of carrying out V-CIP.

question: How long must an NBFC keep customer identification and address records?
expected_answer: At least five years after the business relationship has ended.
evidence_quote: preserve the records pertaining to the identification of the customers and their addresses, obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, for at least five years after the business relationship has ended;

question: Where must an NBFC report the digital lending apps (DLAs) it uses?
expected_answer: On the Reserve Bank's Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) portal, covering both its own DLAs and those of its LSPs.
evidence_quote: An NBFC shall report all DLAs deployed / joined by them, whether their own or those of the LSPs, either exclusively or as a platform participant, on the Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) portal of the Reserve Bank

question: In what forms can an NBFC accept a DLG?
expected_answer: Only as (1) cash deposited with the NBFC, (2) a fixed deposit with a Scheduled Commercial Bank with a lien in the NBFC's favour, or (3) a bank guarantee in the NBFC's favour.
evidence_quote: (1) Cash deposited with the NBFC. (2) Fixed Deposit maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank with a lien marked in favour of the NBFC. (3) Bank Guarantee in favour of the NBFC.

question: For accounts opened with Aadhaar OTP e-KYC, what happens to deposit and borrowal accounts if full CDD is not completed within one year?
expected_answer: Deposit accounts must be closed immediately. Borrowal accounts must allow no further debits.
evidence_quote: (a) in respect of deposit accounts, the NBFC shall close the same immediately, and (b) in respect of borrowal accounts, the NBFC shall allow no further debits.

question: After the periodic KYC due date passes, how many reminders must an NBFC send, and how many must be by letter?
expected_answer: At least three reminders, of which at least one must be by letter.
evidence_quote: Subsequent to the due date, the NBFC shall give at least three reminders, including at least one reminder by letter, at appropriate intervals

question: Under the simplified procedure (small accounts), what are the balance and yearly credit limits?
expected_answer: Total balance across all accounts cannot exceed Rs 50,000 at any time, and total credits cannot exceed Rs 1 lakh in a year.
evidence_quote: (iv) Balances in all their accounts taken together shall not exceed ₹ 50,000 at any point of time. (v) The total credit in all the accounts taken together shall not exceed Rupees One Lakh in a year.

question: For a small account, at what balance or yearly credit level must the NBFC warn the customer to submit KYC documents?
expected_answer: When the balance reaches Rs 40,000 or the total credit in a year reaches Rs 80,000.
evidence_quote: The NBFC shall notify the customer when the balance reaches ₹40,000 or the total credit in a year reaches ₹ 80,000 that appropriate documents for conducting the KYC must be submitted

question: When an LSP works with multiple lenders, what must the digital view of matching loan offers show?
expected_answer: Name(s) of the lender(s), loan amount and tenor, APR, monthly repayment obligation, and penal charges (if any).
evidence_quote: The digital view of loan offers from matching lenders shall include the name (s) of the lender (s) extending the loan offer, amount and tenor of loan, APR, monthly repayment obligation and penal charges (if applicable)

question: Which phone resources can a digital lending app access, and on what conditions?
expected_answer: Only one-time access to camera, microphone, location or another needed facility, only for onboarding/KYC, and only with the borrower's explicit consent.
evidence_quote: A one-time access can be taken for camera, microphone, location or any other facility necessary for the purpose of on- boarding / KYC requirements only, with the explicit consent of the borrower.

question: When entering or renewing a DLG arrangement, what must the DLG provider's declaration contain and who must certify it?
expected_answer: It must be certified by the DLG provider's statutory auditor and state the total DLG amount outstanding, the number of lenders, and the number of portfolios covered.
evidence_quote: a declaration from the DLG provider, certified by the statutory auditor of the DLG provider, on the aggregate DLG amount outstanding, the number of lenders and the respective number of portfolios against which DLG has been provided.

question: How often must LSPs with DLG arrangements publish their DLG disclosures, and what is the deadline?
expected_answer: Monthly, no later than 7 working days after the end of each month.
evidence_quote: Disclosure under sub-paragraph (1) above shall be made on a monthly basis, with the disclosure for any given month to be provided no later than seven (7) working days following the conclusion of that month.

question: Where must the contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officers be displayed?
expected_answer: On the websites of the NBFC and its LSP, on the DLA, and in the KFS given to the borrower.
evidence_quote: Contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officers shall be prominently displayed on the websites of the NBFC, its LSP and on the DLA, as well as in the KFS provided to the borrower.

question: If only a customer's address changes during KYC updation, how and within what time must the NBFC verify the new address?
expected_answer: Through positive confirmation within two months, e.g. an address verification letter, contact point verification or deliverables.
evidence_quote: shall verify the declared address through positive confirmation within two months, by means such as address verification letter, contact point verification, deliverables, etc.

question: For a trust customer, who must be identified as beneficial owners?
expected_answer: The author of the trust, the trustee, beneficiaries with 10% or more interest, and any other natural person with ultimate effective control over the trust.
evidence_quote: the identification of beneficial owner(s) shall include identification of the author of the trust, the trustee, the beneficiaries with 10 percent or more interest in the trust and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the trust

question: What must an NBFC's policy lay down before entering a DLG arrangement?
expected_answer: Eligibility criteria for the DLG provider, the nature and extent of DLG cover, the process for monitoring and reviewing the arrangement, and details of any fees payable to/received by the DLG provider.
evidence_quote: the eligibility criteria for DLG provider, nature and extent of DLG cover, process of monitoring and reviewing the DLG arrangement, and the details of the fees, if any, payable to/ received by the DLG provider

question: What details must the contract between an NBFC and a DLG provider contain?
expected_answer: At least: the extent of DLG cover, the form in which the cover is kept with the NBFC, the timeline for invoking the DLG, and the disclosure requirements under para 28.
evidence_quote: (1) Extent of DLG cover. (2) Form in which DLG cover is to be maintained with the NBFC. (3) Timeline for DLG invocation. (4) Disclosure requirements as under paragraph 28 of these Directions.

question: Who decides the cooling-off period for digital loans, and did this change from the Digital Lending Directions 2025 to the NBFC Credit Facilities Directions 2025?
expected_answer: Earlier the Board of the lender set it in the loan policy; now the NBFC sets it in its credit policy. The minimum of one day did not change.
evidence_quote: The cooling off period shall be determined by the NBFC in terms of their credit policy, subject to the period so determined not being less than one day. | The cooling off period shall be determined by the Board of the RE as laid down in their loan policy, subject to the period so determined not being less than one day.

question: How did the rule on NPA recognition for loans under a DLG change?
expected_answer: The old Digital Lending Directions made the lender responsible for NPA recognition regardless of DLG cover. In the NBFC Credit Facilities Directions this paragraph was substituted with effect from 13 February 2026; it now refers asset classification and provisioning to the NBFC IRACP Directions.
evidence_quote: Substituted w.e.f. February 13, 2026, vide Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Amendment Directions, 2026 dated February 13, 2026 | shall be the responsibility of the RE as per the extant asset classification and provisioning norms irrespective of any DLG cover available at the portfolio level.

question: Are the earlier credit facility directions (including the Digital Lending Directions 2025) still in force for NBFCs?
expected_answer: No. The NBFC Credit Facilities Directions 2025 repealed the existing credit facility directions for NBFCs (notification of 28 Nov 2025). Digital lending rules for NBFCs are now in its Chapter III.
evidence_quote: With the issue of these Directions, the existing Directions, instructions, and guidelines relating to credit facilities for Non-Banking Financial Companies, stand repealed, as communicated vide notification dated November 28, 2025.

question: What is the deadline to implement the due-notice (advance intimation and reminder) requirement for periodic KYC, and did it change in the NBFC KYC Directions 2025?
